# Canary full context

Updated: 2026-10-04

Version 3.17 adds a durable owner watchlist, read-only volume-turn observations,
standard-call discovery, setup coverage and entry markouts through the CLI and
typed Go reads. Setup parameters are unvalidated observations, and historical
reconstruction does not establish what was known at the original decision.
Markouts use later quotes for qualifying Canary-placed fills, exclude commissions
and never replace account P/L; missed targets stay missing. These setup tools
have no MCP surface. Watchlist edits change local preferences only.
CLI and read-only MCP add indicative borrowing-rate discovery, dated price and
liquidity context, and FINRA short-interest screens. Borrower costs are not
lender yields. FINRA positions are twice-monthly reports; percentage of free
float remains unavailable. Source dates and partial market coverage stay visible.
The sweep remains off by default. Owner commissioning requires calibrated
reserves and current native settlement evidence; missing evidence holds the
sweep. Bills can lose value on an early sale. Installation does not enable
automatic submission or grant broker-write permission.

Canary is a local risk desk for a brokerage account, built as a Go daemon, a
shell CLI, a read-only stdio MCP server, a Claude Desktop MCPB, a Claude Code
plugin, a paired app, and a clean-room TWS protocol library. It works with
Interactive Brokers today (IB Gateway or TWS); the broker layer is a separate
Go package, `github.com/osauer/canary/v2/pkg/ibkr`, so other platforms can
follow. The daemon owns the broker connection, account scope, runtime state,
data-source health, market sensors, rulebook, protection proposals, and
option-exercise opportunities. Other surfaces adapt that typed authority rather
than recreating it.

Canary is an independent personal project by Oliver Sauer.

Canary v3.16.0 adds lending observations to the signed binaries and MCPB.
The read-only `canary lending fees --json` command and `canary_lending_fees`
MCP tool expose bounded customer net-fee history from retained IBKR statements. The app shows
dated position loan annotations and expandable fees; Desk's analyst can read
the same evidence. Missing sections, partial coverage and complete zero are
distinct. Participation stays with IBKR. Fees are not added to account P&L:
payment status and P&L/accrual linkage remain unproved. Populated account reports
are still needed for commissioning. Borrow Fee Details describes short-borrow
costs; it is not earned lending income. Forex P&L Details describes currency
transactions and realised lots; it is not the valuation contribution reported
by `canary reporting fx`.
See https://osauer.dev/canary/docs/understand/edge.html#stock-lending-income.

Canary v3.16.0 adds FX contribution to the signed binaries and MCPB.
`canary reporting fx`, `canary_reporting_fx` and Desk's Portfolio → Performance
→ FX expose the same result.
It attributes completed statement-day P&L to currencies in the account's base
currency for Day, WTD, MTD and YTD. It reconciles FX plus other P&L to portfolio
value change after external flows. Partial periods expose missing dates and
omit totals; this is valuation attribution, not realised tax-lot P&L.
See https://osauer.dev/canary/docs/start/reporting.html#fx-contribution.

Data comes from the user's own TWS or IB Gateway session. Availability and
freshness therefore depend on session state, market hours, broker entitlements,
and upstream sources. A delayed, held, fallback, partial, or unavailable result
must retain its data quality, warning code, freshness, source health, and session
context; returning a value does not make a fallback green.

The public project home is https://osauer.dev/canary/. The source repository is
https://github.com/osauer/canary.

## Safety boundary

Standard installer, MCPB, and plain `canary` downloads contain no compiled
broker-write path. The MCP server has no settings-write, order-preview, order
placement, modification, cancellation, or exercise tools, and no resource
subscriptions.

The separate opt-in `canary-trading` tarballs add constrained CLI and app broker
actions. A trading action still requires the matching build, verified account
and mode pins, fresh confirmation or preflight where applicable, journal health,
daemon authorization, and `trading.freeze=false`. No release command or agent
instruction grants a broker write. Trading builds also support explicitly pre-authorised defensive proposals within the existing policy and execution gates.

## Install and version lines

Product v3 installs from signed release assets:

```sh
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/osauer/canary/main/install.sh | sh
canary setup claude-desktop
```

The public Go module intentionally remains `github.com/osauer/canary/v2`: its
root package is the daemon client, `canarytest` its test double, and `pkg/ibkr`
the TWS wire protocol. Its semantic-version authority is the maintained v2 tag
line. `go install github.com/osauer/canary/v2/cmd/canary@latest`
therefore installs the newest compatible v2 module tag, not a root product v3
tag. Product v3 users should use the installer or signed release assets.

The updater stays within the installed product major. Stable v2 maintenance is
cut from `release/2.x`; product v3 and later are cut from `main`.

## MCP tools

Run the server with `canary mcp`. It exposes these read-only tools:

- `canary_status`: daemon, gateway, storage, and source health.
- `canary_data_health`: passive service-health report with source clocks, restrictions and retry state; paginate with its revision.
- `canary_data_check`: coalesced bounded check of required ordinary quote feeds; no subscription purchases or settings changes.
- `canary_trading_status`: pinned broker-write readiness and blockers.
- `canary_settings`: platform settings and observed data quality; no writes.
- `canary_orders_open`: current-context local order lifecycle.
- `canary_orders_history`: bounded local order-journal history.
- `canary_order_status`: typed lifecycle evidence for one journaled order.
- `canary_account`: account financials with field-level authority.
- `canary_positions`: held positions and exposure with account authority.
- `canary_portfolio`: signed allocation by asset class and GICS sector as a share of net liquidation, with index-fund look-through and valuation coverage.
- `canary_recon_status`: redacted statement acquisition and reconciliation health.
- `canary_market`: benchmark and held-underlying quotes with actual contract identity.
- `canary_market_history`: bounded observed underlying bars for charts.
- `canary_calendar`: exchange sessions, holidays, and upcoming closures.
- `canary_macro`: cached official economic calendars and publications with source health.
- `canary_strategies`: current held-option strategy grouping; no order actions.
- `canary_technical`: daily technical evidence for explicitly named symbols.
- `canary_regime`: all eight market indicators, cluster confirmation, and source health.
- `canary_stress`: full portfolio-stress assessment with risk evidence and source health.
- `canary_brief`: current daemon-composed desk summary and Action Queue.
- `canary_reporting`: redacted broker-reporting setup and evidence status.
- `canary_reporting_performance`: retained statement equity series with dated external flows and year-to-date income sums; computes no return.
- `canary_reporting_fx` (since v3.16.0): completed statement-day FX contribution, period coverage and dated gaps; read-only, with no backfill trigger.
- `canary_lending_fees` (since v3.16.0): bounded earned net-fee history, with coverage and unproved payment/P&L linkage; no broker changes.
- `canary_lending_rates`: dated indicative borrower costs for explicitly named US stocks; not earned lender income.
- `canary_lending_screen`: broader borrowing-fee discovery with filters before the result limit, source dates and coverage.
- `canary_lending_market`: bounded cached price and liquidity context; partial or unavailable fields retain their source clocks.
- `canary_short_interest_screen`: FINRA reported short shares and days to cover, with twice-monthly settlement dates; no percentage of free float.
- `canary_edge`: retrospective stock/ETF decision impact and separate option actuals.
- `canary_rules`: ranked rulebook findings, explicit unknown inputs, and the limits in force with their source.
- `canary_proposals`: read-only close/reduce protection candidates.
- `canary_opportunities`: read-only held-option exercise candidates.

Breadth, gamma, and corporate-event engines remain internal daemon inputs.
Regime and Stress provide detailed CLI/MCP reads, while Brief remains the summary.
Regime/Stress history is still retired. Policy and detailed reconciliation reads
remain CLI-only governance surfaces; MCP provides reconciliation status.

## CLI workflow

Useful read-only commands include:

```sh
canary status
canary account
canary positions --by underlying
canary technical AAPL,MSFT
canary brief
canary regime --explain
canary stress --details
canary rules
canary rules policy
canary policy show
canary recon show
canary reporting fx --json # since v3.16.0
canary lending fees --json  # since v3.16.0
canary watchlist list --json
canary setups coverage --json
canary setups markouts --json
canary lending screen --json
canary short-interest screen --json
canary strategies list
canary proposals list
canary opportunities list
canary orders open
canary settings
```

The generated CLI reference is the command authority. The app adds the morning
brief and converged Action Queue, current and recovered alerts, constrained order
surfaces, option-exercise confirmation, data-quality disclosure, settings, and
mobile navigation.

## Requirements

- macOS or Linux; Windows is supported through WSL only.
- IB Gateway 10.37+ or TWS running locally with TWS API access enabled.
- IBKR market-data entitlements for real-time sources the workflow needs.

The daemon auto-discovers common local ports and uses a local Unix-socket RPC
surface. Raw account identifiers and broker credentials do not go to a hosted
Canary service.

Good descriptions say Canary reports the evidence currently available and names
what is stale, degraded, held, blocked, or unknown. Do not claim a fallback is
live, that an MCP client has order authority, that a v3 product tag makes the
`/v2` Go module v3, or that an app/CLI review authorizes a trade.
